chunks: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:

"Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, wiping the outer part of his feet, I would have thought that their inner part was more deserving of wiping than their outer part."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: A title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful.
key_terms.بَاطِنَهُمَا: Their inner side; here, the soles of the feet.
key_terms.بِالْمَسْحِ: By wiping; the act of masah in wudu (ablution).
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose practice establishes the ruling.
key_terms.ظَاهِرَ: The outer or upper surface; here, the top of the feet.
key_terms.يَمْسَحُ: He wipes; here it refers to wiping in wudu (ablution).

ai.seo_question: Why are the tops of the feet wiped in wudu (ablution) instead of the soles?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the legal manner of wiping the feet in wudu (ablution), showing that the outward surface of the feet is to be wiped. It also shows that the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is the basis for the ruling, even where personal reasoning might suggest otherwise.
